chunks: And it was narrated from Muyassir, the seller of al-Zuṭṭī cloth, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: We purchase goods on credit, then a man comes and says, “For how much did it stand against you?” So I say, “It stood at such-and-such,” and I sell it to him at a profit.
He عليه السلام said: “If you sell it as murābaḥah, then he is entitled to the same credit period that you have.”

He said: So I uttered istirjāʿ and said, “We are ruined!” He عليه السلام said: “From what?” I said: “Because every garment on the earth that I sell as murābaḥah is bought from me, and even if I were to reduce from the principal so that I say: it stood at such-and-such.”

He said: When he saw what had become difficult for me, he said: “Shall I not open for you a door in which there will be relief for you?” I said: “Yes.” He عليه السلام said: “Say: ‘It cost me such-and-such, and I sell it to you for such-and-such,’ and do not say: ‘at a profit.’”

key_terms.بِنَظِرَةٍ: on deferred payment or credit term
key_terms.تَقَوَّمَ: was assessed or stood at a given cost
key_terms.رَأْسِ الْمَالِ: the principal capital or original cost
key_terms.فَرَجٌ: relief or ease through a lawful solution
key_terms.مُرَابَحَةً: a sale conducted on a declared profit basis over cost

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling goods bought on credit through murabaha in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a commercial ruling concerning selling goods acquired on credit through murābaḥah. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام explains that if the seller uses the formula of profit-based sale, the buyer shares the same deferred term; he then teaches an alternative wording that avoids invoking murābaḥah explicitly.
